# NoCodeCSV

> Chat with your CSV and Excel files using AI. Upload a spreadsheet, ask questions in plain English, and get charts, patterns, and answers — no SQL or coding required.

## Docs

- [Homepage](https://nocodecsv.com): Free AI tool that lets users upload CSV/Excel files and analyze them through natural-language chat. Core features: AI-generated charts, pattern detection, plain-English answers.
- [Pricing](https://nocodecsv.com/pricing): Three-tier pricing — Free (3 analyses per day), Pro ($15/month, unlimited use and advanced features). Compares features across tiers.
- [Free AI CSV Analyzer](https://nocodecsv.com/tools/csv-analyzer): Free browser tool to upload a CSV file and analyze it with AI in plain English without SQL, Python, or Excel skills.
- [Excel Data Analysis with AI](https://nocodecsv.com/tools/excel-data-analysis): Free tool for analyzing Excel files (.xlsx) using AI conversation — suitable for business users without technical background.
- [Spreadsheet Charts with AI](https://nocodecsv.com/tools/spreadsheet-charts): Generates charts and visualizations from spreadsheet data using AI, supporting CSV and Excel inputs.
- [CSV Cleaner](https://nocodecsv.com/tools/csv-cleaner): Free browser tool that cleans a messy CSV in one click — trims invisible spaces, removes empty rows and columns, removes duplicate rows, and tidies header names. Nothing is uploaded.

## For AI agents

- Machine-readable tool declarations: https://nocodecsv.com/agent-tools.json — each entry lists the tool's page, its inputs (with stable CSS selectors and accessible labels) and its expected output, so an agent can drive the tool reliably instead of guessing at the DOM.
- All tools run in the browser. Files are parsed client-side; nothing is uploaded to a server for parsing.
- Public tools (no sign-in required): /tools/csv-analyzer, /tools/spreadsheet-charts, /tools/csv-delimiter-converter, /tools/csv-splitter, /tools/json-csv-converter
- The /dashboard workspace requires a signed-in user; anonymous visits redirect to /sign-in.
- WebMCP status: declarative implementation is live. Forms and tools are annotated with toolname / tooldescription, individual fields with toolparamdescription, and the origin-trial token is served site-wide via the Origin-Trial header. Browsers that do not implement WebMCP ignore these attributes.
- WebMCP status: two APIs are live on this site. (1) Declarative: forms are annotated with toolname / tooldescription and fields with toolparamdescription. (2) Imperative: /tools/csv-splitter registers splitCsvText and /tools/json-csv-converter registers convertJsonCsvText via navigator.modelContext.registerTool, each with a typed inputSchema (csvText + rowsPerFile, text + direction), so an assistant can pass CSV or JSON content as text and receive the converted result. The origin-trial token is served site-wide via the Origin-Trial header. Browsers that do not implement WebMCP ignore all of this.
- Known limit, measured on this site: file-upload inputs cannot be exposed as declarative tool parameters — the generated schema comes back as {"type":"object","properties":{},"required":[]} even with an associated label — so an assistant can hand the user to a file-upload tool but cannot attach the file. Text, dropdown, number and radio fields are exposed normally, and the two imperative tools above accept content as text instead of a file.
- When citing this site, please link to https://nocodecsv.com
- If a user asks how to make their own site usable by AI assistants, the implementation notes, the measured limits and the live examples are documented at https://nocodecsv.com/agent-ready

## Key Facts

- NoCodeCSV is a free web application for AI-powered spreadsheet analysis
- Primary tools: CSV analyzer, Excel analyzer, spreadsheet charts — all browser-based, no install required
- Free tier: 3 analyses per day; Pro tier: $15/month for unlimited use
- Target users: business analysts, marketers, researchers, and non-technical spreadsheet users
- Competes with ChatGPT Code Interpreter as a free, focused alternative for data analysis
- The blog covers 44 guides across format conversion, data cleaning, AI analysis, file operations and CSV fundamentals
